title: Augustine of Hippo: A Biography
author: Peter Brown
target_audience: Scholars and students of theology, philosophy, and history
Readers interested in Christian history and the late Roman Empire
General readers seeking a well-researched, narrative biography
Anyone interested in Western intellectual and religious traditions
core_themes: Intersection of faith, reason, and personal experience
The social, political, and cultural world of late antiquity
The formation of Christian doctrine and identity
primary_purpose: To provide a comprehensive, nuanced, and scholarly account of the life, times, and influence of Augustine of Hippo, contextualizing his personal journey, intellectual evolution, and enduring legacy within the broader history of late antiquity and the development of Christianity.

structure_format.narrative_style: Scholarly yet accessible; analytical and interpretive; narrative-driven biography
structure_format.organization: Chronological structure tracing Augustine’s early life, conversion, episcopal career, writings, and legacy
features: Engagement with Augustine’s writings (Confessions, City of God, etc.)
Inclusion of revised scholarship and new perspectives in the 2000 edition

key_concepts_lessons: The complexities of personal transformation in the context of historical and cultural upheaval.
The interplay between personal experience (Augustine’s Confessions) and broader theological development.
Understanding how Augustine’s philosophical and theological positions were shaped by—and helped shape—the late Roman world.
How individual lives can catalyze enduring change in religious thought and cultural identity.
The ongoing relevance and reinterpretation of Augustine’s works in subsequent centuries.
notable_features: Regarded as the definitive modern biography of Augustine
Integrates social and cultural contexts with personal narrative
Revised edition incorporates new research and critical perspectives
Balances historical rigor with compelling storytelling
Highlights Augustine's complexities and enduring influence
cultural_historical_context: Originally published in 1967 and revised in 2000, Peter Brown’s biography pioneered a new era of patristic studies by situating Augustine within the turbulent world of late antiquity—a time of social transformation, declining Roman authority, and the solidification of Christian orthodoxy. The book has since become a foundational text in both historical and religious scholarship.
reception_impact: Widely acclaimed as a landmark in historical biography and religious scholarship
Credited with reshaping the modern understanding of Augustine and late antiquity
Highly influential among historians, theologians, and general readers
Praised for narrative skill, depth of insight, and ability to humanize a complex historical figure
comparable_titles: The Confessions of Saint Augustine (primary source)
The City of God by Augustine (primary source)
